common_targets.decision_clock: after official close value for session t is published and available
common_targets.label_rule: FLAT if abs(r)<=1e-8; UP if r>1e-8; DOWN if r< -1e-8
common_targets.eligible_output: three probabilities ordered DOWN, FLAT, UP and summing to 1 within 1e-8
common_targets.brier_formula: sum_k((p_k - I[y=k])^2) over DOWN, FLAT, UP, no division by class count
common_targets.baseline: expanding training-only class frequency with Laplace alpha=1, recomputed causally at every decision time
common_targets.evaluation_alignment: all candidates at a given horizon use identical decision timestamps and label endpoints

paper_native_tasks.rule: Record each native target, split, horizon and metric with source locators. If source definition is ambiguous, mark AMBIGUOUS or BLOCKED_METHOD. Native paper-reported metrics may be descriptive; do not pool incompatible label schemas or endpoints into the common family.
examples: Mehtab-Sen one-week close_norm prediction and binary movement classification
Cureus next-session open/close price tasks and native 5/10/20-year windows
IJSDR claimed next-30-day prediction with undefined accuracy
JRFM next-30-day price task and BE-LSTM
ISMLA option-like dataset with unresolved target schema

point_in_time_rules.daily_ohlcv: Available only after the official close value is published; pre-close decisions use the last completed session.
point_in_time_rules.training_label_end: Every training row label_endpoint_timestamp must be strictly earlier than the decision_timestamp.
point_in_time_rules.fii_dii: Use publication/availability timestamp, not only event date; rows without defensible timestamp require a predeclared lag or exclusion.
point_in_time_rules.vix_options: Snapshot captured no later than decision cutoff; contract and expiry mapping must be point-in-time.
point_in_time_rules.news_social: Both original publication timestamp and ingestion timestamp must precede cutoff; date-only same-day items are excluded unless a fixed lag is predeclared; revisions do not backdate availability.
point_in_time_rules.revisions: Preserve vintage metadata; if history cannot be reconstructed, mark adapted/limited rather than exact PIT replication.

inference.test: one-sided familywise max-studentized-mean-improvement test; positive improvement favors the candidate
inference.observed_statistic: For each candidate j, SE_boot[j] is the sample standard deviation of its 10000 bootstrapped means from the null-centered loss differentials. T_obs=max_j(mean(d[,j])/SE_boot[j]). All candidate/horizon loss differentials are defined on the same fixed family-specific decision-origin rows.
inference.null_centering: Before resampling, for every candidate j form d0[i,j]=d[i,j]-mean(d[,j]); resample d0 under the zero-mean null
inference.resampling: Within each inferential family, freeze one common ordered decision-origin index shared by every candidate and horizon in that family. Use a moving-block bootstrap over those origins. In each replicate, use the same sampled block indexes for all candidates and horizons to preserve paired and cross-horizon dependence. Every planned candidate/horizon must have a finite prediction and loss on the common index; otherwise the family is incomplete.
inference.block_length_sessions: Use one block length per family: max(5, maximum forecast horizon in that family). Thus the common 1/2/3/5/10-session direction and close-regression families use 10 sessions; the one-session next-open family uses 5 sessions. A separately authorized native-horizon family uses max(5, its longest horizon). Do not use different block lengths inside one max-statistic family.
inference.bootstrap_statistic: For each replicate b, compute mean(d0_star[,j]) for every candidate j using the same sampled block origins; T_star[b]=max_j(mean(d0_star[,j])/SE_boot[j]). Reject only when the one-sided max-statistic tail probability is <= 0.05.
inference.simultaneous_95pct_ci: Let c95 be the 95th percentile of max_j(abs(mean(d0_star[,j])/SE_boot[j])) across the null-centered block replicates. The familywise simultaneous interval for candidate j is mean(d[,j]) +/- c95*SE_boot[j]. Report the raw paired mean loss improvement and interval even when the family test is non-significant. Any ordinary unadjusted percentile interval is descriptive only.
inference.missing_candidate_rule: Before the first fit, PPR-4 must finalize an eligible model/pipeline/horizon manifest and common evaluation-origin index using data coverage and point-in-time evidence only, with no prediction outcomes inspected. Source/config rows failing data or method gates are explicitly BLOCKED_DATA/BLOCKED_METHOD before the final PPR4 execution manifest; they are not quietly dropped post-result. Within every inferential family defined by that final manifest, all candidates must have finite predictions/losses on the same common origins; if a planned candidate in that frozen family lacks sufficient common rows, finite predictions/losses, or positive finite SE, mark the whole family INCOMPLETE_NOT_PROMOTABLE and do not issue a confirmatory p-value or promote a candidate.
inference.undefined_metrics: Store null with reason code; never coerce undefined values to zero or silently drop a planned candidate.
inference.repeated_evaluation_rule: No additions to confirmatory families after any evaluation outcome is inspected; amendments are exploratory unless reviewed before the first fit.
inference.family_membership: Each base configuration row is assigned exactly one task_type and target_schema_id. The direction family contains only the fixed three-class DOWN/FLAT/UP Brier task; each regression family contains only its fixed target and absolute-error loss. Within a family, include every pre-frozen configuration × feature pipeline × horizon candidate. Do not combine binary and three-class labels, or regression and classification loss, in the same max-statistic family.

search_bounds.budget_rule: PPR-3 freezes at most 93 base configuration rows across all target/output schemas, four feature-pipeline classes and five common horizons. Conservative upper bound: 93x4x5=1860 outer cells; up to three predeclared seeds gives 5580 outer fit calls. Tuning is capped at 20 candidate cells x 20 inner settings x (up to five chronological folds plus one refit)=2400 additional fit calls. Combined upper bound is 7980, within the global 8000-call cap. The current matrix has 71 active candidate rows and 1183 feature-pipeline/horizon cells, so its conservative 3-seed outer fit cap is 3549; the 12 predeclared tuning cells require at most 936 additional calls under their specified 18/8-setting grids. The current configuration plan is therefore at most 4485 fit calls. Count a fit call as one top-level estimator fit for one specified cell/seed; the manifest must separately record any calibration or preprocessing estimator fit. All fitting is on the purged training prefix; one outer fit per cell/seed is used for the frozen PPR3 validation segment. Blocked/out-of-scope rows execute zero fits. If a candidate is added after outcomes are inspected, it is exploratory and needs a new protocol amendment.
search_bounds.configuration_unit: A base configuration row is a unique estimator/architecture + task_type/target_schema + required model setting combination, before expansion over feature pipeline and horizon. The total of these rows across all target types is at most 80. If an estimator is used for a different target/output schema, that is a separate row and consumes the same cap.

evaluation_protocol.eligible_development_panel: Only source- and PIT-valid decision origins that remain outside the sealed final holdout, as proven by a pre-existing holdout metadata/manifest. PPR-4 must verify the exclusion before any modelling. If it cannot be verified without opening holdout observations or labels, PPR-4 is blocked.
evaluation_protocol.split: After restricting to eligible development origins, sort by official NSE session and split chronologically: first 80% of eligible origins for training, following 20% for validation. No shuffle. Freeze the row-ID lists and hashes in the PPR-4 manifest before fitting.
evaluation_protocol.training_purge: For every training observation, label_endpoint_timestamp must be strictly earlier than the first validation decision timestamp. Purge rows whose label endpoints overlap or reach the validation interval. Fit scalers, imputers, feature selection, text aggregation/model mapping, calibrators and hyperparameters using training history only.
evaluation_protocol.fit_cadence: Fit each candidate/configuration × eligible feature pipeline × horizon × predeclared seed once on the purged training prefix. Keep learned model parameters frozen through the validation block. Feature values at each validation decision may update only from point-in-time inputs available by that decision. No refits on validation observations.
evaluation_protocol.cadence_deviation: This PPR3 benchmark intentionally differs from the existing Phase 7 method specification that refits every 20 trading sessions. Record separate results and do not compare its performance metrics as if the refit cadence were identical. A single frozen validation fit is selected to provide a bounded common comparison across many source-derived models and to keep the pre-registered fit-call budget finite.
evaluation_protocol.row_alignment: Within each inferential family, freeze one ordered validation decision-origin index common to every candidate/pipeline/horizon. Use the same date rows even where some output horizons mature later; each target endpoint must be observed before the sealed holdout boundary. If the common set has fewer than 250 origins, mark the family NOT_ESTIMABLE and do not promote a model.
evaluation_protocol.final_holdout: The final untouched holdout is explicitly excluded from the PPR3 panel, split calculation, feature coverage choice, hyperparameter tuning, model selection, and all reported PPR3 metrics. Do not inspect its observations or labels.
evaluation_protocol.refit_policy: No repeated 20-session refits, no periodic retuning, and no test-block updates to model parameters. Online training-rate baseline updates may use only labels whose endpoint is strictly earlier than the current decision time.
evaluation_protocol.reproducibility: Record eligible panel row IDs, split boundary, decision-origin index, label endpoint per horizon, holdout-exclusion proof, source cache digests, preprocessing parameters and fit count before permitting execution.
